rule: S_N must not be null
rationale: S_N is the primary identifier and join key for the table. It is a mandatory field with 0% missing values in the sample.

rule: S_N must exist in Acc_Info_dirty.S_N
rationale: S_N is designated as a one-to-one join key with Acc_Info_dirty.S_N. Referential integrity must be enforced to ensure every customer biography record has a corresponding account record.

rule: Account_No must not be null
rationale: Account_No is a mandatory business identifier linking to account information. The sample shows 0% missing values.

rule: Account_No must be exactly 4 digits
rationale: Account numbers follow a 4-digit numeric format (range 1001-1028). Values must be convertible to string and match the 4-digit pattern.

rule: Name must be in Title Case (allowing for lowercase particles like bin, binte, s/o, d/o)
rationale: 93.3% of names follow Title Case convention. Values like 'lim wei jie' (all lowercase) and 'WANG SHI JIE' (all uppercase) deviate from the standard format.

check_params.logic: any(w[0].islower() or w.isupper() for w in str(row['Name']).split() if w.lower() not in ('bin','binte','d/o','s/o') and len(w) > 1)

rule: ID_No must follow Singapore NRIC/FIN format: one prefix letter (S, T, F, or G), followed by exactly 7 digits, and ending with one uppercase checksum letter
rationale: 93.3% of values conform to the standard Singapore NRIC/FIN format. Anomalous formats like '1916569C' (missing prefix) and 'F212233V' (6 digits) must be flagged.

rule: ID_No must match the corresponding ID value in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: ID_No and Acc_Info_dirty.ID represent the same national identifier for a customer. For the same S_N, these values must be consistent across tables.

check_params.semantic_check: ID_No must exactly match the ID value in the sibling table

rule: Race must be one of: Chinese, Malay, Indian
rationale: The dataset contains only these three semantic race categories. Casing variations (MALAY, malay, indian) represent the same values and should be standardized, but the validation enforces the canonical set.

rule: Gender must be either Male or Female
rationale: The column represents binary gender classification with observed values Male/Female (plus case variants). The canonical values are Male and Female.

rule: Age must be between 0 and 120 inclusive
rationale: Age represents human age in years. Values must be non-negative and within realistic human lifespan. The sample contains invalid values -5 and 4 (below service threshold) and 66 (valid).

rule: Age must be parseable as a numeric value
rationale: The Age column is intended to be numeric but contains text values like 'Twenty-five' that cannot be parsed as numbers. This rule flags any non-numeric representation.

rule: Contact_No must not be null
rationale: Contact number is a critical field with 6.7% missing values observed in the sample. As a mandatory contact field, null values are not permitted.

rule: Contact_No must be a valid Singapore phone number with 8 digits (starting with 6, 8, or 9), optionally prefixed with +65 or 65
rationale: All customers are located in Singapore. Valid numbers are 8 digits starting with 6 (landline), 8 or 9 (mobile). The sample contains an invalid 7-digit number '8964359'.

rule: Email must not be null
rationale: Email is a mandatory contact field with 0% missing values in the sample.

rule: Email must contain exactly one @ symbol with no spaces and valid local-part and domain structure
rationale: The sample contains structurally malformed emails: 'not-an-email' (no @), 'useremail.com' (no @), 'zx91 @example.com' (embedded space), 'nabilah@@example.com' (consecutive @).

rule: Country must represent Singapore (allowing for known variants: Singapore, SINGAPORE, singapore, S'pore, SG, Singapura, Republic of Singapore, 新加坡)
rationale: The dataset description confirms all customers are located in Singapore. The 8 observed values are all variants of Singapore. Any other value indicates a data error.

check_params.logic: str(row['Country']).strip() not in ['Singapore', 'SINGAPORE', 'singapore', 'S\'pore', 'SG', 'Singapura', 'Republic of Singapore', '新加坡']

rule: Street_Name must be in Title Case
rationale: 96.7% of street names follow Title Case. One value 'HOLLAND ROAD' uses all caps and deviates from the standard format.

check_params.logic: any(w[0].islower() or w.isupper() for w in str(row['Street_Name']).split() if len(w) > 1)

rule: Postal_Code must be a 6-digit code
rationale: Singapore postal codes are 6-digit numbers. The column is stored as int64 causing loss of leading zeros. Values like 6907 (4 digits) and 99999 (5 digits) are invalid lengths.

rule: Gender must be consistent with name particles: 'Bin' or 's/o' indicates Male; 'Binte' or 'd/o' indicates Female
rationale: Malay and Indian naming conventions use specific particles that encode gender. 'Bin' and 's/o' (son of) are male indicators; 'Binte' and 'd/o' (daughter of) are female indicators. Mismatches indicate data inconsistency.

check_params.logic: (any(p in ' ' + str(row['Name']).lower() + ' ' for p in [' bin ', ' s/o ']) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'male') or (any(p in ' ' + str(row['Name']).lower() + ' ' for p in [' binte ', ' d/o ']) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'female')

rule: S_N must be unique within Cust_Bio_dirty (one-to-one join key)
rationale: One-to-one key relationship detected by MinHash analysis; duplicate values break the join.

rule: Account_No must be unique within Cust_Bio_dirty
rationale: Column is 93.3% distinct with duplicate value(s) [1001, 1010] observed; treated as a candidate identifier — duplicates flagged for review.

rule: ID_No must be unique within Cust_Bio_dirty
rationale: Column is 96.7% distinct with duplicate value(s) ['F1011121T'] observed; treated as a candidate identifier — duplicates flagged for review.

rule: Email must be unique within Cust_Bio_dirty
rationale: Column is 96.7% distinct with duplicate value(s) ['thm@example.com'] observed; treated as a candidate identifier — duplicates flagged for review.
